transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Avery Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Quantaco ML Eng), Rosa Martinez (Quantaco Product), Noah Patel (Quantaco Infra), Maya Singh (Quantaco DS)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in for Quantaco focusing on cost/unit economics (tokens/sec/$), caching benefits, and batching tradeoffs. Reviewed latest Redwood benchmarks, discussed realistic production traffic shapes, and aligned on next steps: share configs, run dedicated benchmarks, and validate latency SLOs.

00:00 - 00:30 - Avery: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um quick roll call?
00:30 - 01:10 - Liam: yep, hi this is Liam, Rosa, Noah and Maya are here too, good to go.
01:10 - 02:05 - Avery: cool. agenda today is cost econ, we sent the updated spreadsheet, we'll walk through the numbers, show the bench slides, then talk tradeoffs and action items
02:05 - 03:20 - Samira: just to set expectations, the numbers we have are from a mix of hosted runs and a small dedicated pool emulation. there is noise, but you can see directional trends
03:20 - 04:00 - Rosa: quick question — when you say tokens/sec/$ can you clarify the numerator/denominator? we've seen variations in different reports
04:00 - 05:05 - Diego: yeah good point. our shorthand tokens/sec/$ is throughput normalized by hourly cost — effectively tokens produced per second per dollar of hourly committed cost; it's a way to compare raw throughput/unit-cost across hardware and model variants. not perfect but useful for tradeoffs
05:05 - 06:30 - Maya: ok makes sense, can you give the headline numbers?
06:30 - 09:10 - Samira: sure. on hosted (our multi-tenant GPU pools) for the Llama-2-70B-like model with 512 context we measured roughly 850 tokens/sec/$ at our default batching; on a small dedicated 8xA100 pool with aggressive batching and KV/prefix cache we hit about 3,200 tokens/sec/$ — so about ~3.7x improvement. numbers depend a lot on batch size and cache hit-rate
09:10 - 10:00 - Liam: 3.2k sounds great. what's tail latency at that throughput?
10:00 - 12:20 - Samira: right, tradeoff — when pushing batch sizes to maximize tokens/sec you see P95 climb. at batch size 64 our P50 was ~70ms token latency, P95 ~360ms; at batch 16 P50 ~50ms, P95 ~180ms. target SLO you mentioned was 200ms P95, correct?
12:20 - 13:00 - Liam: yes 200ms commercially for interactive features.
13:00 - 15:20 - Diego: and caching helps — if you have repeated prefixes, KV/prefix cache can reduce compute by ~25-40% depending on hit rate; in our pilot traces we saw an average hit-rate ~28% which translated to ~30% cost reduction in tokens/sec/$ effective improvement
15:20 - 16:00 - Maya: how are you modeling cache warmup and TTLs?
16:00 - 18:10 - Samira: in the spreadsheet we include a warmup factor and separate scenarios: cold start, steady-state with 20/30/40% hit rates. TTL depends on workload, we modeled 5-20 minute TTLs for session-style usage. worth testing with your own traces
18:10 - 20:00 - Rosa: regarding batch sizing, we have some very spiky traffic — small bursts of concurrent requests — won't that hurt batching efficiency?
20:00 - 22:10 - Diego: yes, spiky traffic reduces batching aggregation. our routing supports dynamic batching windows and we can bias routing toward dedicated pool for predictable throughput. also prefix caching is independent and helps even with smaller batches
22:10 - 24:00 - Noah: network-wise we need to make sure our VPC peering and egress won't add jitter; we'll validate that during dedicated test
24:00 - 26:40 - Samira: we proposed three benchmark configs in the doc: 1) interactive steady-state (QPS constant), 2) spiky bursty traffic (Poisson bursts), 3) session-local prefix-heavy workload. each will report tokens/sec/$, P50/P95, and cost per 1M tokens
26:40 - 28:00 - Liam: can you remind us the cost-per-1M tokens number for hosted vs dedicated from the sheet?
28:00 - 30:10 - Samira: hosted was around $0.95 per 1M tokens for this model at baseline batching; dedicated optimized was about $0.27 per 1M tokens when amortized across sustained utilization and with conservative cache assumptions in the model
30:10 - 31:40 - Rosa: big delta. how much of that is just the reserved commitment pricing vs technical throughput?
31:40 - 33:05 - Diego: it's both. reserved pricing and better packing of hardware, lower multi-tenant overhead, plus more aggressive batching and kernel-level optimizations. Quantaco's utilization profile matters a lot — if you can't sustain utilization you'd lose some benefits of dedicated
33:05 - 35:20 - Maya: what about quantization impact? we tried 4-bit and saw some quality regressions on a subset, does Redwood's cost model account for quantization choices?
35:20 - 37:00 - Samira: yes we have rows for fp16, 8-bit, and 4-bit-like quant profiles; 4-bit improves tokens/sec/$ further but we flag quality/regression risk. we can run evals on your prompt set to show delta
37:00 - 38:30 - Liam: ok please do that. also can we get a per-route cost breakdown, like embedding vs generation per call?
38:30 - 40:10 - Diego: yep Redwood Console can show token-level cost and route breakdowns; we'll export sample dashboards and a per-route CSV for your routes
40:10 - 42:00 - Rosa: on the caching side, any changes needed to our app? how do we surface cacheable prefixes?
42:00 - 44:00 - Samira: minimal — we support prefix registration and metadata headers. typical flow: you register session prefix or hashed context, Redwood will attempt KV-cache hits. we'll share docs and example instrumentation snippet
44:00 - 46:10 - Noah: action item for infra — we'll confirm VPC peering, NAT config, and egress rules and share constraints by next week
46:10 - 47:30 - Avery: recap — Redwood sends updated cost model + bench configs, Quantaco to run internal evals with prefix cache enabled and provide prompt samples, then we'll schedule a dedicated bench window. Does that match?
47:30 - 48:00 - Liam: yes that matches, thanks everyone
48:00 - 49:00 - Avery: great, we'll follow up in email with dates. end
